title: Salaries in Lunceford's band
summary: Young earned $10 a night on one-nighters, Willie Smith more, and Sy Oliver was paid $5 for arranging and copying "Blue Heaven."

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: After Jimmie Lunceford we were talking about Comparative (inaudible) salaries, and you mentioned before how much you made when you were with Earl, how much when you were on the road and how much when you were at the Grand Terrace. How about with Lunceford?
Well, Lunceford was kind of tight with that buck, you know, and I'm -- we didn't make -- at least I
didn't make so much money. Willie Smith was top man in Lunceford's band, and I don't know what Willie made, but I understand he was getting around $100.00 a week.

Well, when I went with Lunceford on the one nighters, I was getting $10.00 a night, and that was pro rata. If I worked seven nights, I got $70.00, and that was it. Now, Willie, as I say, Willie Smith was top man. He made a little more money than that. I guess he made about, well, about $12.00 or $13.00 a night. He had been with him a while, and he was the star over there. He was top man in the band. But --
Did the other members of the band, did (inaudible) they make --
They didn't make a lot. I know Sy Oliver made the arrangement of Blue Heaven for $5.00, and he didn't only make the arrangement, he copied it off for $5.00.
Sy told me this, you know, so I know this to be a fact.

Money -- we didn't make money, you know, in them -- in fact, this is one of the things that contributed to finally that band disbanding, most of the top guys in that band, because they knew that somebody was making money because they were selling too many records for somebody not to --
The money was going to Lunceford or --
Well, I don't know. We -- one time we didn't know who it was going -- but we heard later that Oxley
took Lunceford too, that Lunceford was taking us, but Oxley was taking Lunceford now. I don't -- I never did get the truth of this, but I know somebody was taking somebody down the line.
